requirements.discrimination: Invalid history is rejected with a field-specific error before any independently logged provider request or callback, leaves history empty, and preserves first-turn seeding; accepted history is snapshotted.

Caller, built-in and MCP effects remain absent until visible approval; allow/deny/cancel/invalid/timeout/unavailable decisions are settled and late allowance cannot execute refused work. Descriptive safety metadata cannot grant authority.
All three executor sources receive visible calls, correlated single resolutions and a real pre-effect veto; effect ledgers prove refused work does not occur.
Each source-named tool call is observed while the independent effect ledger is empty, approval precedes execution, and missing/reordered/duplicate pairs fail the shared event validator.
Exactly one observed executor performs each approved effect: caller process identity matches Node, MCP identity differs, and a built-in shell writes its own effect; denied tools produce no work.
A single provider request advertises caller, built-in and configured MCP tools together without duplicate names; each selected call identifies its matching executor source.
Registered schemas reach the provider intact; missing dialects, invalid schemas and invalid executors fail construction. Descriptive safety metadata is accepted without bypassing approval.
Every callback error remains terminal under stop; malformed, miscorrelated and duplicate results or unavailable callbacks stay terminal under continue and issue no extra provider request.

Caller, built-in and MCP failed/unknown effects retain one truthful resolution under both policies. Continuing provider messages carry full correlated errors and every captured partial stdout/stderr or MCP content; failed/unknown cannot become completed after a successful final response.
Completed, failed, cancelled and unknown outcomes each retain one call/result pair; malformed and duplicate submissions terminate without a second public settlement.

After uncertainty caller, shell, write, MCP, delegate and skill effects stay blocked, including previously pending approval. Started root/nested effects drain to actual completion; blocked errors identify the original call and prescribe inspection/new-turn work. Local inspection retains both approval and skill guards; accepted cancellation cannot recover.

Continue cannot bypass malformed, duplicate, miscorrelated or unavailable callback results; four actual skill guard failures and accepted cancellation remain terminal. Inspection refusals cannot reach another provider completion, while every executor source retains its ordinary approval failure semantics.

Independent effect ledgers and callback counts reject retries or fictitious rollback; failed and uncertain outcomes remain distinct across all executors. Real late callback successes injected after settlement cannot add a second result, alter recorded history or change provider replay; nested and in-flight effects settle truthfully.

Repeated unchanged invalid configuration/history/content is nonretryable with field-specific repair instructions and no provider work. Applying the repair permits work; a transient retryable provider failure succeeds only on an explicit identical caller request. Uncertain effects prescribe inspection before new-turn work and are never retried automatically; native errors retain the full remedy and retryability.
